purpose: Distinguish the raw-window gain's relationship to unfused content versus the number of attended spatial memory keys.
method: Use the same 16,384 represented-spatial-feature admission policy, insurance reserve, protected prompts, early points, multi-scale anchor and indexed RoPE as the raw-window candidate. At each read attend only to the two newest retained nonconditioning entries as raw features, matching the fused arm's oldest-skeleton-plus-newest entry count; no EMA fusion. This is an experimental matched-read-size control, not a proposed replacement for the token-budgeted storage policy. No new confidence gate, threshold, redetection, training or labels at inference.
validation: Two independent seq3 no-op and two active gates must reproduce, satisfy budget/write/pointer checks and record the two-entry raw read. Two independent short seq23 cropped gates must match. Only then run seq23 with the same cropped input and prompt and compare it to the already audited fused and raw-window arms. Verify attention-key counts rather than assuming equal sizes.
limitations: This is a selected sequence and a full-video system-level comparison: model predictions and future memory selections can diverge, so it is not a same-state causal ablation. A fixed two-entry read is an engineering control and does not satisfy the user's requested token-window policy on its own.
